source: The average register of these 80 songs, from 2019, is 5.95 (on a scale of 1 to 10).
claim: The 80 songs from 2019 have an average vocal register of 5.95.

source: Yet when it comes to 2019, men's voices in pop music are much lower than the ‘70s and ‘80s.
claim: The 2019 average register of 5.95 is below the 1970s average of 6.60 and the 1980s average of 6.92.

source: And I wasn't expecting to see such a clear trend: rising register until the early ‘90s and then a drop-off.
claim: The yearly average register reaches its highest value, 7.08, in 1990 and its lowest, 5.72, in 2017.

source: Up until the the late 1980s, men's voices were steadily shifting higher.
claim: Average register rose from 5.77 in the 1950s to 6.15 in the 1960s, 6.60 in the 1970s and 6.92 in the 1980s.

source: Here is how that compares to 2017, one of the years with the lowest average register in our dataset.
claim: 2017 has the lowest average register of any year, at 5.72.

source: Note how, in 2017, fewer songs have a register of 7 or higher.
claim: Of the top 100 songs in each year, 70 in 1984 and 32 in 2017 had a register of 7 or higher.

source: 2019 is the big circle on the upper right, the highest register in 60 years.
claim: The average register of top-10 hits in 2019 was 7.6, the highest of any year in the data, above 1988's 7.21.

source: If we remove any song that did not hit the top 10, we're left with 5 songs, and four of those have a high register, such as Khalid's Talk.
claim: Of the 5 songs from 2019 that reached the top 10, 4 have a register of 7 or higher.

source: Let's look at the first clear spike in register: 1970.
claim: The average register rose by 0.23 in 1970, the largest one-year increase up to that point, versus 0.19 in 1963.

source: Currently playing is "Sherry" by the 4 Seasons from 1962, a low year for register.
claim: 1962's average register of 5.84 was lower than 1961's 5.98 and 1963's 6.03.
